Is it customary in some places to use an apostrophe where a comma might be used like in the title portion of "1'840" vice "1,840"?

No, not yet, but it will be. It just makes more sense. Think of it this way, apostrophes are used to separate many things that should still be together, like in contractions:

  • can't
  • won't
  • didn't

Or in languages that have glottal stops in the words:

  • Hawai'i
  • Maʻafala
  • Punctuation Shaker - TV Tropes

Most English speakers demarcate numbers with commas, like this: 1,000,000. Europeans demarcate numbers with periods, like this: 1.000.000. But both commas and periods are used to demarcate sentences and sentence fragments (phrases). Periods and commas are NEVER used to separate anything, except decimals. So, to eliminate ambiguity, I use apostrophes. With the apostrophe in 1'840, it looks like somebody made art using old pennies dated 1840. See how well apostrophes eliminate ambiguities? Everybody will be doing it my way eventually.
